sections.h2: What should Binghamton owners know before putting a house on the market?
sections.html:
Binghamton is the seat of Broome County, and a sale here involves the city for permits, Broome County for tax collection and recording, and a housing market priced well below the rest of New York. The Census Bureau estimates 46,418 residents for July 1, 2025, a drop of 3.1% from the 2020 estimates base.

The Census figures for 2020 to 2024 put the typical owned home at $124,800 and typical rent at $870 a month, and only 44.0% of the 21,393 households own. Most Binghamton households rent rather than own.

The sections below cover the city's setting, how weather and floods affect houses, who bills property tax, which permits matter and what it costs to record a deed in Broome County.

sections.h2: Where is Binghamton and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Binghamton sits in the Southern Tier near the Pennsylvania border, in a valley where the Chenango River meets the Susquehanna. The city covers 10.48 square miles of land, which works out to 4,577.6 people per square mile, and downtown is at about 860 feet while hillside homes climb past 1,800 feet.

The settlement began as Chenango Point and took its name from William Bingham, a Philadelphian who bought the land patent in 1786. It became a village in 1834 and a city in 1867. Canal and railroad connections drew cigar makers and then the Endicott Johnson shoe company. IBM was founded in the greater Binghamton area, and the flight simulator was invented in the city. At its peak, around the mid-1950s, the population was about 85,000.

The old grid laid out near the rivers gives way to curving streets on the Southside hills. Historic districts include the Railroad Terminal Historic District and the Abel Bennett Tract on the West Side, and landmark or historic-district buildings go through design review before demolition.

sections.h2: How do floods and winter weather affect a Binghamton house?
sections.html:
Floods are part of the city's record: major floods hit in 1865, 1935, 1936, 2006 and 2011. After the 1935 and 1936 events the city built flood walls along the Susquehanna and Chenango, and Broome County maintains 17.5 miles of levees, many of them in Binghamton.

  • Expect buyers near the rivers to ask about basement water, sump pumps and any past repairs. Gather receipts before you list.
  • Yearly snowfall averages 86.5 inches, with about 164 days of measurable precipitation, so roof condition, gutters and heating systems get close attention in an inspection.

A house with water damage, an old furnace or a tired roof is a common reason owners here look at selling as-is rather than paying for repairs first.

sections.h2: What does the local economy mean for Binghamton house values?
sections.html:
The region built its wealth on manufacturing and lost much of it after the Cold War, and electronics and defense work has been shrinking since 1990. Education and health care now carry the city. Binghamton University, Broome Community College, United Health Services and Lourdes Hospital are major employers in the area.

The Census figures show the result: median household income of $45,578, per capita income of $30,320 and a poverty rate of 32.6%. About 30.7% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree. The mean commute is only 19.0 minutes, and 79.8% of residents had the same address a year earlier.

With values this low, a realistic price for your block depends on recent sales nearby, so look at your own street before relying on any citywide figure.

sections.h2: Who collects Binghamton property tax, and how do you contest an assessment?
sections.html:
Broome County collects it. The City Treasurer no longer collects property and school taxes, and the county's tax office also handles in-rem foreclosures, bankruptcies and tax certificates for the city and the Binghamton City School District.

The City Assessor handles assessments. Grievance Day for 2026 was May 26, 2026, and a complaint had to be filed by then on form RP-524 with the city's review board. That deadline has passed, so for 2027 ask the Assessor's Office for the new date and file before it.

If back taxes are the reason you are selling, note that the county runs an installment program for delinquent owners in danger of foreclosure. It requires 25% down and 24 monthly payments at 1% monthly interest, and all new taxes must be paid on time during the plan. A sale that pays the balance at closing ends the problem sooner.

sections.h2: Which permits and housing programs affect a Binghamton sale?
sections.html:
The Building Construction and Code Enforcement office requires a building permit under Section 200-9 of the city code for construction, alteration, removal, demolition and work on electrical, plumbing and HVAC systems. A permit must be on display before work begins.

  • Plumbing work in every kind of occupancy, including one- and two-family homes, must be done by a licensed Master Plumber.
  • Demolition and work that affects a structural element need a permit, and landmark or historic-district buildings go through the Commission on Architecture and Urban Design first.
  • Street work, including a dumpster in the public right of way, needs a separate permit from the Department of Engineering.

The city's First-Time Homebuyer Program gives deferred loans of up to $10,000 for down payment and closing costs. If title to the home is sold or transferred within 5 years, or it stops being the owner's principal residence, the whole loan comes due. After 5 years it is forgiven. If you bought through this program, expect a payoff at closing and ask the Housing Division for the figure.

sections.h2: What are the Broome County recording costs for a Binghamton deed?
sections.html:
Recording happens at the Broome County Clerk's office in the County Office Building on Hawley Street, and the clerk estimates about $190 for a standard two-page residential deed once the state forms are counted. Sellers sign the deed before a notary, and the TP-584 and RP-5217 must be signed by both seller and buyer.

Broome County Clerk fees for a residential deed
ItemFee
Deed$45 plus $5 per page
Transfer tax return (TP-584)$10 filing fee plus tax owed
Real property transfer report (RP-5217)$125 for residential property
Transfer tax in Broome County$5 per $1,000 ($4 state, $1 county)

Source: Broome County Clerk, Deed FAQs. Round an uneven price up to the next $500 before applying the rate, so a $175,100 sale is taxed as $175,500. A seller who lives out of state also completes form IT-2663 for estimated income tax. The clerk's Fraud Alert service emails you when a document is recorded under your name, which is useful once the house is sold.

sections.h2: What choices does a Binghamton seller have?
sections.html:
An agent listing, a private sale and a cash purchase all work here, and the right choice turns on what shape the house is in and how soon you need to close. Listing suits a turnkey single-family home on a quiet block. A cash sale suits a house with flood history, a vacant two-family with code issues, or an inherited property that you would rather not renovate.

Before you accept any figure, pull the assessed value and recent comparable sales, price out the repairs a buyer would ask for, and confirm what, if anything, you owe in back taxes or program loans.

faqs.q: Where do Binghamton tax payments go?
faqs.a: Pay Broome County's Real Property Tax Services. The county is the collection agent for the City of Binghamton and the Binghamton City School District, so the city treasurer no longer takes tax payments. Mail goes to the county's post office box in Binghamton, and you can also pay in person.

faqs.q: Is Binghamton Grievance Day still open?
faqs.a: No. Grievance Day for 2026 was May 26, 2026, and the filing deadline that day was 4:30 pm. For the next cycle, call the City Assessor's Office for the date and file form RP-524 before it.

faqs.q: What happens to my first-time homebuyer loan if I sell?
faqs.a: The full loan becomes due. Under the city's program, selling or transferring title within 5 years, or moving out of the home, makes 100% repayable. After 5 years the deferred loan is forgiven in full.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax will I pay selling in Binghamton?
faqs.a: Expect $5 per $1,000 of the price in Broome County, rounded up to the next $500. The state takes $4 of that and the county $1. A $120,000 sale produces $600. Houses at $1 million or more add a 1% buyer-paid tax.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed for repairs before I sell my Binghamton house?
faqs.a: Yes, for most structural, electrical, plumbing and HVAC work. Section 200-9 of the city code requires a building permit displayed on site before work starts. Plumbing must be done by a licensed Master Plumber, and historic-district buildings get design review first.
